task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: Series-level AVOID share vs winning: rho=-0.26, p=0.07, n=50; underpowered; confounded by team quality. Requires ~80 series for p<0.05.
On-ball defensive scheme labeling rates very low (14.9% for Detroit, 3.3% for Orlando); high label error risk; limited sample for classification.
No leakage found in predictive pipeline, but external constants could carry implicit information.
Post-hoc narrative judged adaptation; unclear mechanism; limited sample of 10 series.

failed_approaches.why: Low labeling rates and label error; insufficient data to reliably classify suppression tactics.
Small sample size, confounding by team strength; results inconclusive.

evidence_establishes: Labeling of suppression-related defensive actions is difficult and low in coverage; prior series-level analysis found a negative association but was underpowered and confounded.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning; no robust, powered, and unbiased study exists for this specific question.
own_inferences: Given only 54 series, the effective sample for a series-level logistic regression is too small to detect even moderate effects; labeling challenges further reduce usable observations; therefore a definitive test is infeasible with current data.
uncertainties: Exact effect size of suppression mix on series win; potential for unmeasured confounders such as coaching strategies, injuries; possibility of improving labels via advanced ML; data completeness across seasons.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical studies demonstrate labeling challenges and underpowered series analyses, leading to the conclusion that the question cannot be reliably answered with the available data.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 54 series available, insufficient power for moderate effect sizes.
Low coverage and high error rates in labeling suppression actions.
Team quality and other strategic variables confound the relationship.

prior_work.summary: Prior work attempted to relate suppression tactics to outcomes but faced labeling and power issues; no definitive conclusion.

risks.text: Limited number of series reduces ability to detect effects.
Inaccurate or sparse labeling of suppression actions.
Team skill and other strategic factors may drive observed associations.
Potential for future data leakage if not careful in model training.

design.estimand: Effect of suppression-conditional recommended mix on probability of winning a playoff series
design.power: Underpowered for moderate effects; would need ~80 series for 80% power at alpha=0.05
design.controls: Team win probability, coaching changes, injury rates
design.falsification: Compare to a dummy variable of random defensive mix
design.decision_rule: If estimated odds ratio >1.5 and p<0.05 after controls, support; else reject
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons, per-game and possession-level data
